judgments.reasoning_cat1: The term is definite (six years, 31 March 1987 to 30 March 1993), but the self-definition "The Contract shall be the present contract with the changes made by this Memorandum" leaves the composite instrument's content to be assembled by inference.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: Checked against para. 14 (c018), which keeps the 1981-84 booklet and all side agreements alive, and para. 15 (c019), which promises a later consolidated document; identifying what "the Contract" is at any moment therefore depends on harmonising three provisions.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: "[A]n additional $3.67 per shift from wages and after taxes (maximum of five (5) shifts) shall be contributed to the Welfare Fund" does not say who contributes or on what base, and "Pension and welfare contributions shall be made on this amount" leaves "this amount" and the contribution base open — the core of a welfare-fund contribution dispute.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: It must be read with the Section 13-H.1 amendments (c038 changing the rate to 7.678%, c039 inserting the same $3.67 after-tax deduction) and with Earnings Bonus para. 8 (c055), which expressly bars Welfare Fund contributions on the $25.93 add-back; the three do not obviously fit together.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: A bare schedule of dated dollar increases to the journeyman day scale; nothing but OCR noise clouds the figures.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: It sits comfortably beside 2(a) (c002) and the COLA clause (c004); no other provision contradicts the increase amounts.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: "[P]ursuant to the relevant provisions of the Contract" does not identify which provisions govern the COLA computation, and the bracketed index sentence reads as an editorial insertion of uncertain operative force.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: The incorporated "relevant provisions" live in the 1981-84 booklet preserved by para. 14 (c018), which is outside this document, so the fit cannot be verified from the instrument itself.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: The opening sentence is incomplete ("shall have full force and effect at the Edison, New Jersey by The Times within the Northeast Corridor"), and it layers vague standards — "every effort shall be made," "to the extent practicable," layoff protection "because of the introduction of automated processes" — on top of a broad arbitration commitment.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: Its promise that the arbitrator "shall issue his award before operations commence" is immediately qualified by the interim-ruling sentence within the same paragraph, and the layoff protection interacts with the staffing changes in Appendix A (c021-c022).

judgments.reasoning_cat1: The most-favoured-nation trigger turns on a "wage and benefit package which is additional to or different from that contained herein" not "granted in exchange for productivity improvements or attrition" nor "diverted from an existing or subsequently negotiated" package — evaluative terms with no metric — and the parenthetical list of nine unions raises an expressio unius question about other bargaining units.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: It overlaps with Earnings Bonus para. 7 (c054), which lets the Union apply $25.93 to any fringe benefit "negotiated by any other union and the Times," so the two adoption mechanisms could yield double counting.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: "[S]uch agreements and such documents, including but not limited to group contracts and trust agreements ... as are necessary to administer" is an open-ended catch-all whose reach beyond the enumerated documents is undefined.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: Paragraph 5(c) (c009) expressly caps the obligation at contributions "required by the Contract," which pulls against an unlimited duty to execute whatever trust documents the Fund deems necessary — a live tension in a contribution dispute.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: The pension analogue of 5(a), with the same "including but not limited to ... as are necessary" catch-all but a narrower enumerated list (Pension Plan and trust agreement).
judgments.reasoning_cat2: Same interaction with 5(c) (c009) capping expenditure, and the asymmetry between the 5(a) and 5(b) lists invites an argument that different documents are covered.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: "[B]eyond its obligation to make contributions required by the Contract for The Times deliverers" is the limiting phrase, and both the measure of that obligation and the class of "Times deliverers" (regulars, extras, casuals) are left undefined.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: It is the express limit on paras. 5(a)-(b) (c007-c008) and must also be squared with the contribution obligations in 2(a) (c002), 13-H.1 (c038-c040) and the Earnings Bonus carve-out (c055).

judgments.reasoning_cat1: A one-line pointer to Appendix A; nothing in the wording is capable of two readings.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: Appendix A (c021-c024) exists and matches the description, so the cross-reference resolves.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: The protected characteristics are a closed enumeration (color, race, sex, religion, national origin), inviting an expressio unius argument that age, disability and others are excluded, though the clause is otherwise plain.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: Nothing else in the Memorandum addresses discrimination; para. 14 (c018) simply preserves the balance of Section 4.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: A single numeric increase from $60,000 to $75,000 in a named CBA section; no term is capable of competing readings.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: No other provision touches AD&D coverage; para. 14 (c018) leaves the rest of Section 3-H.2 intact.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: "Group I employees not so scheduled" contains a dangling reference — nothing earlier in the Memorandum says what they are or are not scheduled for — so the class entitled to averaged jury pay cannot be identified from the text.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: The missing antecedent lives in Section 13-J of the 1981-84 agreement preserved by para. 14 (c018), so the provision cannot be applied from this instrument alone.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: "[T]here shall be a foreman or assistant foreman in each plant" gives the Publisher a choice between the two, and "Whenever the Publisher has one or more Plants" is surplusage; the obligation is nevertheless plain.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: No staffing provision elsewhere (Appendix A, c021-c023) contradicts a per-plant supervisor requirement.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: A bare undertaking to provide a letter attached as Appendix C; the operative content is in the appendix, not here.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: Appendix C (c030) is in fact attached and matches, though a promise to "provide a letter" rather than to perform its terms could be argued to be less than a covenant.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: A pointer to a letter of interpretation attached as Appendix D; nothing in the sentence bears two meanings.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: Appendix D (c031-c032) is attached and corresponds to the description.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: The sentence is definite as an undertaking to execute a letter, but the substantive designations of "Status Quo" and Merits Arbitrators are not stated.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: The attached Appendix E (c034) never mentions "Status Quo" or Merits arbitrators at all — it only records that neutrals were identified and a meeting will occur — so the cross-reference does not deliver what para. 13 describes.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: "All dates in the Contract shall be updated to reflect this Memorandum of Agreement" is an instruction without a rule for how updating is done, and the survival list ends in a broad sweep of "all terms and conditions contained in the 1981-84 contract booklet."
judgments.reasoning_cat2: This is the priority clause for the whole instrument, so any inconsistency elsewhere — the West Side Directs abolition in Appendix B (c026) versus the confirming letter (c059), or para. 15's new document (c019) — is resolved through it.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: "Promptly" is soft, and "embodying the provisions contained in the Contract as modified" leaves the drafting task open, but the obligation itself is clear.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: If the consolidated New York Times Agreement is executed it competes with this Memorandum and the 1981-84 booklet preserved by para. 14 (c018), raising a question about which text governs.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: A single effective-date sentence keyed to Union ratification; nothing is capable of two readings.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: Several substantive terms are made effective 31 March 1987 with retroactive payments (c002), so "effective immediately following Union ratification" and the retroactivity provisions must be read together.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: The chapeau makes the whole of Appendix A "[s]ubject to there being no increase in the number of floor hires as set forth in the Collective Bargaining Agreement" while the very next words create ten additional floor regular situations — a condition that sits awkwardly against the grant.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: It must be reconciled with the layoff and job-placement protections in para. 3 (c005) and with sub-paragraph B (c022), which adds five further floor situations under the same cap.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: The clause is a specific enumeration of new situations and chauffeur slots; "five additional chauffeurs on dayside (4 days and Monday night)" is compressed but identifiable.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: It shares the "no increase in floor hires" condition in the chapeau of paragraph 1 (c021), so the same cap question applies to it.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: One sentence creating one regular situation for the third recovery car; no term admits of competing readings.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: Nothing elsewhere in Appendix A or the Memorandum addresses recovery cars.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: A ministerial instruction to update names on an existing schedule at pages 104-5 of the 1981-84 agreement.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: It depends on the 1981-84 booklet preserved by para. 14 (c018) but does not contradict anything there.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: "[S]hall continue to be served by" preserves an existing practice without describing it, and "delivery points designated by the Publisher" is an unbounded discretion.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: It sits with the returns provision (c028) and the honor-box side letter (c029) in the same Appendix B; none directly contradicts it.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: It abolishes the 1983 Memorandum outright while granting a reorganisation right subject only to a floor on "the present number of routes," and "this Agreement" is ambiguous as between Appendix B, the Memorandum and the Contract.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: The 9 September 1988 confirming letter (c059) says the "abolition" does not affect any other agreement regarding those routes except the attrition portion, which directly cuts back the word "abolished" here.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: A bare cross-reference to Appendix B-1 with no operative content of its own.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: Appendix B-1 (c029) exists, but its content — "maintain present practices" — is itself supplied only by the Spinelli memorandum (c058), so the chain is longer than the pointer suggests.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: The mail-in rule carries an exception for "unsold current copies on 'bulldog' routes" and an undefined "other designated portion of each copy," and the last sentence preserving "[a]ny existing physical pick-up" pulls against the general rule it follows.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: The reference to "this Contract" here and "this Agreement" in the adjacent West Side clause (c026) use different terms for what may be the same instrument defined in para. 1 (c001).

judgments.reasoning_cat1: "[M]aintain present practices in such deliveries in The Times direct operation" is precisely the kind of undefined phrase whose boundary cannot be applied without extrinsic evidence.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: The Glassman letter and the Spinelli memorandum (c058) were supplied to fix the content of "present practices," but that memorandum describes only the West Side Direct area, which is narrower than "The Times direct operation" in this letter.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: "[S]hall be made available no later than ten (10) days following the end of such payroll week" uses "made available" rather than paid or received, and neither the amount nor the base of the weekly contribution is stated — a timing standard at the heart of a contribution claim.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: It must be read with para. 11 (c015) that merely promises the letter, with 2(a) (c002) fixing the $3.67 per-shift amount, and with the 13-H.1 rate amendments (c038-c040) that set what is to be remitted weekly.
